cards.question: Sum of the first `n` terms of an arithmetic series.
Sum of the first `n` terms of a geometric series.
Sum of an infinite geometric series.
The Pythagorean theorem
cards.answer: `a^2 + b^2 = c^2`, where `c` is the hypotenuse of a right triangle and `a` and `b` are the lengths of the other two sides.

cards.question: Point-Slope Form of the Equation of a line
The Standard Form of the Equation of a Circle
cards.answer:
`(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2`

where `(h, k)` is the center of the circle and `r` is the radius.

cards.question: The definition of a polynomial function of degree `n` with one variable.
cards.answer:
`P(x) = a_n x^n + a_(n-1) x^(n-1)`
`+ a_(n-2) x^(n-2) + ... + a_1 x + a_0`

where `n` is a nonnegative integer, `a_n != 0`, and `a_0, a_1, ..., a_n` are constants.

cards.question:
The Quadratic Formula:

The solutions of the quadratic equation `ax^2 + bx + c = 0` are given by
The Remainder Theorem
cards.answer: If `R` is the remainder when `P(x)` is divided by `x - c`, then `R = P(c)`.

cards.question: The Factor Theorem
cards.answer: The number `c` is a zero of a polynomial `P(x)` if and only if `x - c` is a factor of `P(x)`.

cards.question: The Leading Term Test
cards.answer: For extreme `x`-values of a polynomial, as goes the graph of the leading term (height-wise), so goes the height values of the entire polynomial.

cards.question: The behavior of the graph of `y = P(x)` at its `x`-intercepts
cards.answer:
If the corresponding zero has an odd multiplicity, the graph crosses the `x`-axis at that intercept.

If the corresponding zero has an even multiplicity, the graph touches or "bounces off" the `x`-axis at that intercept.

cards.question:
The Intermediate Value Theorem:

Suppose `P(a) != P(b)`, where `a < b`.
cards.answer:
`P(x)` takes on every value between `P(a)` and `P(b)` on the interval `[a, b]`.

(Note: This implies that if `P(a)` and `P(b)` have opposite signs, there is at least one zero between `a` and `b`.)

cards.question: The Rational Zero Theorem.
cards.answer: If a polynomial `P(x)` has integer coefficients, then every rational zero of `P(x)` is of the form `p/q`, where `p` is a factor of the constant term and `q` is a factor of the leading coefficient.

cards.question: The Conjugate Pairs Theorem.
cards.answer: Suppose `P(x)` has real coefficients, then `a + bi` is a zero of `P(x)` if and only if `a - bi` is also a zero.

cards.question: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra (FTA).
cards.answer: Any polynomial of degree `n >= 1` with complex coefficients has exactly `n` zeros, counting multiplicities.

cards.question: Vertical Asymptotes of a Rational Function `R(x) = (P(x))/(Q(x))`
cards.answer: Occur where `Q(x) = 0` (assuming the numerator and denominator have no common factors).

cards.question: Horizontal Asymptote of a Rational Function `f(x) = (a_n x^n + ...)/(b_m x^m + ...)`
cards.answer:
If `n < m`, the horizontal asymptote is `y = 0`.

If `n = m`, the horizontal asymptote is `y = a_n/b_m`.

If `n > m`, there is no horizontal asymptote.

cards.question: Slant (Oblique) Asymptote of a Rational Function, `R(x) = (P(x))/(Q(x))`
cards.answer:
A rational function has a slant asymptote (SA) if the degree of the numerator is exactly one more than the degree of the denominator.

The equation of the SA is `y = quotient` upon long division of `P(x)` by `Q(x)`.

cards.question: Converting between Degrees and Radians
cards.answer:
To convert degrees to radians, multiply by `pi / 180^circ`.

To convert radians to degrees, multiply by `180^circ / pi`.

cards.question: Arc Length of a Circle
cards.answer:
`s = r theta`

where `r` is the radius and `theta` is the central angle measured in radians.

cards.question: Right Triangle Trigonometric Ratios (SOH CAH TOA)
cards.answer:
`sin(theta) = (opp)/(hyp)`, `csc(theta) = (hyp)/(opp)`

`cos(theta) = (adj)/(hyp)`, `sec(theta) = (hyp)/(adj)`

`tan(theta) = (opp)/(adj)`, `cot(theta) = (adj)/(opp)`

cards.question: Reference Angle Definition
cards.answer: The reference angle `alpha` for any angle `theta` in standard position is the positive acute angle formed by the terminal side of `theta` and the `x`-axis.

cards.question: Wrapping Function
cards.answer:
The wrapping function maps any real number, `t`, to a point on the unit circle via `W(t)=(cos t, sin t)`.

It is used to define the trigonometric functions for any real number, `t`.

cards.question: Even and Odd Properties of Trigonometric Functions
cards.answer:
Even: `cos(-t) = cos(t)` and `sec(-t) = sec(t)`

Odd: `sin(-t) = -sin(t)`, `csc(-t) = -csc(t)`, `tan(-t) = -tan(t)`, `cot(-t) = -cot(t)`

cards.question: Amplitude and Period of `y = a sin(bx)` and `y = a cos(bx)`
cards.answer:
Amplitude: `|a|`

Period: `(2pi) / |b|`

cards.question: Period of Tangent and Cotangent
cards.answer: For `y = a tan(bx)` and `y = a cot(bx)`, the Period is `pi / |b|`.

cards.question: How to find the phase shift for any trig function given by `y = a f(bx - c)`
cards.answer:
Set `bx - c = 0` and solve for `x`.

The phase shift is `c / b`.

cards.question: Reciprocal Identities
cards.answer:
`sin x=1/csc x `

` cos x = 1/sec x `

`tan x = 1/cot x`

cards.question: Ratio Identities
cards.answer:
`tan x = sin x / cos x`

`cot x = cos x / sin x`

cards.question: Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities
cards.answer:
`sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1`

`1 + tan^2 x = sec^2 x`

`1 + cot^2 x = csc^2 x`

cards.question: Sum Identity for Sine
cards.answer:
`sin(alpha + beta) =`

`sin(alpha)cos(beta) + sin(beta)cos(alpha)`

cards.question: Sum Identity for Cosine
cards.answer:
`cos(alpha + beta) =`

`cos(alpha)cos(beta) - sin(alpha)sin(beta)`

cards.question: Sum and Difference Identities for Tangent
cards.answer:
`tan(alpha + beta) = (tan(alpha) + tan(beta)) / (1 - tan(alpha)tan(beta))`

`tan(alpha - beta) = (tan(alpha) - tan(beta)) / (1 + tan(alpha)tan(beta))`

cards.question: Cofunction Identities
cards.answer:
`sin(pi/2 - theta) = cos(theta)`

`cos(pi/2 - theta) = sin(theta)`

`tan(pi/2 - theta) = cot(theta)`

Substitute `pi/2` with `90^circ` to get the cofunction identities in degrees.
